rationale: This is Microsoft's general website Terms of Use rather than a storefront purchase agreement, so it never frames a 'sale' of digital content at all — ownership deception is present only implicitly, via language that treats all software and documents as licensed, never owned. The bigger problems are readability (dense, all-caps legal blocks) and aggressive unilateral clauses: Microsoft can terminate access, remove content, or change the terms at any time without notice, and takes a broad royalty-free license to anything users post.
